claims.text: The magnetocaloric response of as-deposited, non-equiatomic FeMnNiGeSi-type alloys under low-field cycling is governed primarily by crystallographic disorder and grain-boundary density rather than solely by composition or phase purity.
Rapid deposition produces increased crystallographic disorder in FeMnNiGeSi-type alloys.
Rapid deposition produces a finer-grained microstructure in FeMnNiGeSi-type alloys.
Increased crystallographic disorder broadens the magnetostructural transition.
A finer grain structure reduces magnetostructural-transition hysteresis.
Disordered, fine-grained material has a more gradual and less sharply peaked entropy-change response than ordered, single-phase hexagonal bulk material.
The proposed as-deposited thin films or foils possess microstructural disorder and fine grains.
Post-deposition annealing will increase crystallographic order.
Post-deposition annealing will cause grain growth.
Microstructural disorder impedes cooperative magnetostructural transitions.
Grain boundaries impede cooperative magnetostructural transitions.
Ordering and grain growth facilitate sharper, more cooperative magnetostructural transitions.
Annealed samples with increased order and larger grains will exhibit a sharper magnetocaloric entropy-change peak than the as-deposited baseline.
Annealed samples will exhibit a higher-amplitude magnetocaloric entropy change than the as-deposited baseline.
Annealed samples will exhibit greater hysteresis than the as-deposited baseline.
The annealed samples' response will resemble that of bulk arc-melted ingots.
The proposed relationships apply to similar non-equiatomic FeMnNiGeSi-type compositions made by rapid deposition and tested at field changes below 2 T.
